items.label: BillionToOne Q2 FY2026 (08-05-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Oncology catalysts: MolDX Medicare coverage for Northstar Response

set.signal: Oncology catalysts: MolDX Medicare coverage for Northstar Response in the immunotherapy (IO) and IO-combination settings is still expected by the end of this year; Response accounts for almost two-thirds of oncology test volume. The highly sensitive tumor-naive MRD test remains on track to launch by the end of the year. CEO: MRD will launch around the time Response coverage comes in and its volume will not be throttled, so rapid oncology growth can be dilutive to gross margin in the short term.

items.reason: Drop the June 24 Journal of Liquid Biopsy study sentence (142 patients, 570 samples, survival finding): it is a publication readout, and ai_bio publications / trial readouts yield nothing. The coverage and MRD catalysts stay as stated.
items.evidence: On June 24, we published a peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Liquid Biopsy validating NorthStar Response for monitoring immunotherapy and immuno-combination therapy.

items.label: BillionToOne Q2 FY2026 (08-05-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Excluding true-ups, ASP rose $15 quarter over quarter

set.signal: Excluding true-ups, ASP rose $15 quarter over quarter, driven by a record number of payer contracts signed in the quarter; reported ASP fell about $20 sequentially, which management called simply a result of true-up timing (true-up was $49 per test in Q1 versus $14 per test in Q2). Oncology ASPs were unchanged quarter over quarter pending MolDX coverage for Northstar Response, so all sequential oncology growth came from test volume. CEO: BillionToOne bills the vast majority of its tests under its own PLA codes (its carrier-screening PLA code took effect January 2025) rather than bundled or stacked billing, and has not experienced the carrier-screening payer friction that others may be seeing. Management expects overall COGS per test to rise gradually over time as oncology grows faster than prenatal.

items.reason: 'a competitor reported' payer friction is the Jefferies analyst's premise, not management's; replace with the CEO's own hedged words. Also keep management's attribution on the ASP decline ('simply a result of true-up timing') instead of the unattributed 'only because'.
items.evidence: we obtained our PLA code effective January 2025, so we have not experienced the payer friction that others may be seeing on carrier screening.
